newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: New issues sap Zimbabwean shares.
newsitem.headline: New issues sap Zimbabwean shares.

text.p: Zimbabwean shares traded mixed with reasonable turnover in select counters on Tuesday with brokers saying the market was tired on the back of recent new issues.

"The market is very tired because of the new issues. A lot of money is tied up in the new issues and there's not much activity on the market and this trend is going to continue until these new issues are out of the way," one broker said.
The new issues include manufacturing and marketing group Randalls Holdings Ltd which is slotted to make its debut on the Zimbabwe Stock Exchange (ZSE) on April 7.

The key ZSE industrial index rose 39.44 points to close at 10,483.38 on Tuesday after bankers Barclays rose 100 cents to 3,700 and publishers Zimpapers as well as steel window manufacturer Radar gained 50 cents each to 3,700 and 550 respectively.
Horticulture company Ariston also gained 50 cents to 2,400 while 10-cent additions were recorded in pharmaceutical group Caps and finance house UDC at 360.

Among the losers, tyre manufacturer Dunlop shed 20 cents to 210 while engineering group Gulliver at 340, transporter Clan at 220, chemical firm Chloride at 145 and winery Afdis at 490 all lost 10 cents.
Minings were quiet with brokers saying the market was still skittish after last week's news that the Swiss central bank planned to sell some of its gold reserves.
Gold producer Ashanti jumped 500 cents to 10,000 but Wankie Colliery shed 10 cents to 510 leaving the mining index 2.65 points off at 957.07.
